text:
Connor Brown has 5 goals and 10 points in 14 games for New Jersey, and the most talked-about of them was the one Washington complained he kicked in during a three-point night on Nov. 14. He's 32, on his fifth NHL team, and playing about 15.5 minutes as a reliable middle-six winger.

Our numbers say enjoy it but don't bank it. He has 5 goals on 3.15 expected (the quality of his chances) and is shooting 25%, almost double the league's 13.3%. The Devils have also scored 5.2 more goals than expected with him on the ice, while at five on five they get outchanced when he plays (45.9% of expected goals), much worse than when he sits.

His skill shows up in the passing. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 19% of his setups crossing the royal road, the pass that moves a goalie side to side, against 7% for a typical forward. Evolving-Hockey had him worth about one win above replacement last season, which is roughly what he is: a useful player having a lucky stretch.
headline: Connor Brown keeps finding the net
